body:
Sam: I have an ARM first-chunk experiment passing 198 release tests/21 docs on your exact #296 integration. It extends your first-chunk gathering mechanism to retain a contiguous first chunk in the existing stage, then reuses the already-proved ARM many-message kernels. No new public API or assembly in this experiment. Equal-key/equal-length groups are the initial diagnostic case; it establishes the available whole-cycle gain before independent-CV kernels.

Could you make the existing first-chunk-cycle instrument runnable through our Mac runner, preserving its Rust measurement/judge code and fresh alternating layout pairs? The current shell orchestration is Linux-specific (`/root/.cargo/env`, `/proc/cpuinfo`, `taskset`); the native Mac is reached through a trusted `example: host_lab` job, not SSH. An example can launch a committed portable driver, with old/new library worktrees and pinned bench/clocks in its private result directory. Please record P/E cycle counts separately on ARM and retain the existing complete-work boundaries. This is an orchestration adaptation of one instrument, not a second sampler/judge. Name a pushed tip when ready and I can queue it immediately.

Devon has #156's benchmark point for the same basic workload; the wider mixed-mode/sparse matrix still matters for ARM. I am finishing the ring fix/gates while you prepare this. Releases remain held for the ARM wins.

— John Servil

ARM diagnostic tip is pushed: `8652b990eb0d33648277cacd8314fa3e0922d4c9`, branch `probe/arm-first-chunk`, directly against baseline `85c4b2d92b71c87a42261509fa6258f02903a0bc`. 198 release tests/21 docs pass on ARM Linux. No speed claim yet. The native job needs this pushed identity; promotion stays behind the complete-work measurements and full gates.

— John Servil

The ARM experiment now also feeds the existing SME2 message kernel up to 128 compatible messages per call, sharing one streaming-mode entry. It uses the existing 16 KiB threshold and SME2 turn, with NEON for smaller or busy-unit cases. No new assembly. Latest **`7f0d4e35e9dd66cf0c9930594988a034d1c02e44`**, branch `probe/arm-first-chunk`; 198 release tests, 21 docs and check-builds pass, including NEON-only and one-CPU builds. Baseline remains85c4b2d9; earlier8652b990 preserves the NEON-only experiment for a later mechanism comparison. This latest source is the native complete-cycle target. Speed is still unmeasured.

— John Servil

@samshackleton-tech could you take the native Mac orchestration adaptation requested above? The ARM experiment is ready at **7f0d4e35e9dd66cf0c9930594988a034d1c02e44**, baseline85c4b2d9; it reuses the proved NEON/SME2 kernels. The existing runner accepts a pushed library example `host_lab` that can invoke a committed portable driver. Keep your first-chunk-cycle Rust sampler/judge shared, four fresh layout pairs and complete-work costs; report P/E counters separately. The Linux-only shell wrapper is the remaining obstacle to that wider native matrix. I will queue it immediately and keep the VM idle. Please prioritize #295's missing-wrapper mutation gate first.

— John Servil

@samshackleton-tech I am taking the small Mac orchestration wrapper now so the first ARM measurement can proceed while you close #295's mutation coverage. I will reuse the Rust sampler and judge from your pinned first-chunk-cycle script, with load checks and supplemental P/E counters; the existing runner's host_lab entry will launch it. Please use that one adapter when I post it rather than starting another. Current ARM target is **fffe8e13c7a192f019e3a5f24a6e6b09a6067e83**, baseline85c4b2d9. This last refinement selects the equal-length SIMD experiment by plain-mode flags, keeping key values out of dispatcher comparisons; other modes retain correct in-place finishing.

— John Servil

First native ARM result: **2.8–3.5× faster complete receive/update/digest/reset cycles**, using the existing proved NEON/SME2 kernels.

Mac 2015 compared safe baseline `90f78cb46c9adae6e6c4869c4a78597f1350a755` with ARM candidate `6761e7adb748f7d96e5f324a847fb321bb753285`, bench #157 `49f45960ff276558e707cb777a357679332788fe`. Both sides carry byte-identical reviewed ring/fixture files. Four fresh layouts, alternating adjacent pairs; AC power, High Power mode; VM idle. The check reported no slower cell among its eight named points.

For 1,024 messages of 1 KiB, each arriving in four 256-byte pieces (single-threaded, ns per input byte):

| Before each cycle | Before | Candidate | Wall-time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Other work | 0.874 | 0.267 | 69.4% |
| 20 µs idle | 0.850 | 0.243 | 71.4% |
| 5 ms idle | 2.137 | 0.756 | 64.6% |

Multithreaded cells show similar gains. Receive-buffer copies, descriptor refill, all four updates, outputs and reset are inside the operation. The implementation retains the first chunk in the existing stage and finalizes compatible plain messages together. Public APIs, Hasher storage and assembly stay as they were.

The two clocks agree. For example, pair 2's P-core-only 20 µs cell records 3.461 → 0.895 cycles/B beside 0.847 → 0.243 ns/B; instructions are 19.066 → 1.952/B. The 5 ms samples mix P/E cores and lower clocks; their wall-time means retain that cost. Package energy is unavailable here.

Evidence: `runner/results/2015-arm-first-small-arrivals.20261108-004241/`; comparisons use bench-hashes compare. Candidate: 200 ARM release tests and 21 docs pass; earlier build configurations passed. Prototype remains unlanded, with broader shape/mode, mutation and integration gates ahead. Next I will test further headroom and improve the existing mechanism where measurements warrant it. 0.9 remains held for ARM results and releases come from main.

— John Servil

### Shared-path follow-up: reuse the existing kernel directly

Mac2018 compared **b0d716f2e2089642c58fa24e18ba7f6757646b72** with preserved **6761e7adb748f7d96e5f324a847fb321bb753285**, on bench **49f45960ff276558e707cb777a357679332788fe**, four fresh alternating layouts and the same eight named points. The separate-final-block extension was slower in four complete-cycle cells:

| Schedule | ST | MT |
|---|---:|---:|
| Other work between cycles | +14.5% | +14.9% |
| 20 µs idle | +17.5% | +17.0% |

The extension's 203 tests, full build matrix, 128 symbolic cases covering every final-group store count, and 37 rejecting controls pass. Its measured benefit on this workload leaves its extra assembly entry, descriptor, flag and startup check short of their complexity cost. That prototype stays archived.

A fresh contract review found the existing SME2 message kernel already accepts this workload's equal whole-block messages. New probe **df3ad8d14ada924711b532b2ee8da8733bf34419**, organization branch **probe/arm-shared-existing-sme**, routes them through that typed wrapper inside the shared collection path. It writes the caller's canonical output directly. Other lengths keep the general collection path. This reduces the experiment from nine changed files to one Rust file. Assembly and startup code stay as they were. 202 tests, 21 docs and all build configurations pass, including mode, threshold, partial-group and mixed-length route controls.

Mac2019 is now comparing this source with6761 on the same frozen benchmark and points. First stage found no Slower cell. It requested a second stage for two instruction-count suspects and a64B wall-time suspect; that confirmation is still running. The VM stays idle. Eight points leave268points unmeasured, so this remains an experiment rather than a landing verdict.

The original Mac2015 2.8–3.5× complete-cycle result stays preserved. 0.9 remains held.

— John Servil

Mac2019 is complete: **df3ad8d14ada924711b532b2ee8da8733bf34419 passes the scoped native comparison against6761e7ad**, bench49f45960, on AC/High Power. First stage: four fresh paired layouts over eight named points. Confirmation:64freshpairs over the three suspects. Both stages report no Slower cell; confirmation reports no Level-cell instruction suspect under the check's existing consistency rule.

The first-stage complete busy cycle is0.269ns/input-B on both sides. The20us cycle is0.242→0.243. The existing Rust reader/judge produced the summaries; samples retain wall time and per-core-kind counts. The preserved original speed result remains source-specific. This shared-path check adds evidence that the existing kernel can carry the win with one collection mechanism.

Result: runner/results/2019-arm-shared-existing-sme.20261108-041147. Summaries: tmp/arm-study/mac2019-compare.txt andmac2019-second-compare.txt. The broad sparse/startup/partial-length matrix, changed-line mutations and actual integration remain open. Eight named points leave268unmeasured.

— John Servil
